External React and FlatBuffers cases are oracle-assisted file probes, not real retrieval or end-to-end benchmarks.
Role-additive normalization is an experimental prerequisite, not accepted production policy.
No LateOn, fusion, grouped rank, Hit@10, 72-query quality, statistical generalization, index, or production repair is measured.
The shipped order is TOTAL-EVIDENCE-FIRST: matches counts name terms and full source-span terms, including declarations and comments. It is not independent body-only evidence.

role-additive.status: experimental prerequisite, not accepted production policy

orders.name-first: nameMatches descending, matches descending, source startLine ascending (candidate comparator). matches keeps the same total-evidence definition.

unchangedBehavior: at least one non-path matched concept
design.changeBoundary: only the supplement sort comparator and the experimental tokenizer differ in disposable copies; the production-ranking algorithm is not reimplemented
design.suppliedCandidateRule: External files are supplied as retrieval candidates by design, in the frozen order. These are oracle-assisted file-supplement probes, not real retrieval or end-to-end measurements.

declaredScope.comparison: exactly two tokenizers x two sort orders at the existing file-symbol supplementation boundary
declaredScope.s1: actual frozen publication and baseline mcp_fusion input; reproduction of archived baseline and role-additive results required before comparison
declaredScope.external: react and flatbuffers source-backed file-supplement probes with deliberately supplied retrieval candidates; oracle-assisted, not real retrieval or end-to-end benchmarks

caveats: The shipped TOTAL-EVIDENCE-FIRST matches field is a union of name and full source-span terms; declaration and comment text counts.
Eligibility and per-owner matches are tokenizer/query determined; the comparator only reorders, and the script asserts selection, hashes, eligibility, and match evidence are preserved across orders.
Supplied React and FlatBuffers files are retrieval candidates by design. They measure the supplement boundary only.
Recovered Flow parses can omit declarations. A target is unscorable only when missing, span-invalid, or unsupported by its source; recovered status alone is reported, not treated as failure.
S1 rank 17 of 37 is a within-file rank before the six-symbol cut, not a grouped or end-to-end rank.

r1.query: where does React run the cleanup function of useEffect

acceptable.evidence: packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberCommitEffects.js:248 commitHookEffectListUnmount(flags, finishedWork, nearestMountedAncestor); :907 safelyCallDestroy(current, nearestMountedAncestor, destroy)

r1.justification: Effect destroy functions are invoked from commitHookEffectListUnmount/safelyCallDestroy; findings file names ReactFiberCommitEffects.js as the owner.

r2.query: where does useState schedule a re-render when you call the setter
r2.justification: dispatchSetState is the bound setter; it requests a lane and enqueues/schedules the update.

r4.query: where does React warn about a missing key prop

acceptable.evidence: packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactChildFiber.js:151 DEV warnForMissingKey assignment; :1107 warnOnInvalidKey delegates to it

r4.justification: Missing-key warnings are implemented in the reconciler and both server renderers.

r5.query: where does React flush passive effects after a commit

acceptable.evidence: packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.js:4655 flushPendingEffectsDelayed delegates through flushPendingEffects to flushPassiveEffects; :4728 flushPassiveEffectsImpl

r5.justification: Runtime owner of passive-effect flushing; many tests call flushPassiveEffects.

r8.query: where does React bail out of re-rendering a component whose props did not change

r9.query: where does React throw when a hook is called outside a component
r9.justification: Approved owner: throwInvalidHookError / resolveDispatcher; eslint RulesOfHooks and compiler validators are competitors.

fb-object.query: where does the builder finish a table and deduplicate its virtual table

acceptable.evidence: ts/builder.ts endObject writes the vtable and reuses an existing matching vtable

fb-object.justification: endObject closes the table, trims the vtable, and deduplicates it against previously stored vtables.

fb-finish.query: where does the builder finalize a buffer with its root table and file identifier

acceptable.evidence: ts/builder.ts finish writes the optional file identifier and the root table offset

fb-finish.justification: finish writes the file identifier bytes, adds the root table offset, and sets the final position.

fb-string.query: where does the builder encode a UTF8 string and store its terminator

acceptable.evidence: ts/builder.ts createString encodes text to UTF8, adds the zero terminator, and copies the bytes

fb-string.justification: createString encodes the input, appends a zero byte terminator, and writes the bytes into a vector.
